newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Bangui diamond exchange to resume trade soon.
newsitem.headline: Bangui diamond exchange to resume trade soon.

text.p: The Central African Republic's diamond exchange is to resume operations in a few days, state radio reported on Monday.
The move is another sign of a return to normal following implementation of a peace deal to end bloody clashes between disaffected soldiers and African peacekeepers in June.
The radio, which quoted a statement from the mines and energy ministry and the small-scale miners' association, did not specify exactly when the exchange would resume operations.
The idea behind the exchange, launched in February 1996, is to help prospectors secure better prices.

The exchange halted its activities after just two sessions because of three army mutinies in under a year. The last session was in March 1996, before the first of the three mutinies began in May that year.
Diamonds are the impoverished nation's main mineral resource. Output in 1995 was 484,251 carats but smuggling into the neighbouring Congo Republic undermined official trade.
Exports are mainly uncut diamonds. The bourse is open to mining companies, diamond traders, buying officials, diamond cutters and small-scale miners who meet registration requirements.
Other signs of a return to normality include the return of the disaffected soldiers to their units and joint patrols bringing together a reunified army and peacekeepers.
Mali's widely respected former military leader, Amadou Toumani Toure, brokered a January deal to end the mutinies and a fresh deal in July after the clashes with the peacekeepers.
